name: Schengen short-stay visa (Category C)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires showing you'll leave the Schengen area at the end of your visit.
This requires travel health insurance covering at least €30,000, valid across the Schengen area.
requirements.fix_path: Purchase qualifying Schengen travel health insurance before applying.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires showing sufficient funds to cover the visit and return journey.

evidence_required.document: Travel health insurance certificate (€30,000 minimum coverage)
Evidence of sufficient funds and intent to leave

outcome.duration_length: up to 90 days in any 180-day period
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: valid throughout the Schengen area, not just Portugal; cannot be used to establish residence

sources.title: Portal de Vistos - Ministério dos Negócios Estrangeiros

notes: Fee €90 (adult) / €45 (children 6-12) / €35 (visa-facilitation-agreement nationals) confirmed via vistos.mne.gov.pt — same €90 base figure as Germany's Schengen visitor route, consistent since both implement the same EU-wide fee regulation. Approximately 60 nationalities are visa-exempt (US, UK, Brazil, Canada, Australia among them). EES (Entry/Exit System) launched October 2025, replacing manual passport stamping — a genuine operational change relevant to how border crossings are now recorded, though it doesn't change visa eligibility itself. ETIAS (a €20 travel authorization for visa-exempt travellers, analogous to the US ESTA) is expected late 2026 — not yet in force at this verification date, flagged as an imminent rather than current requirement. Structurally identical to de_schengen_visitor in almost every respect since both are the same EU instrument — the main difference is which consulate/VFS centre processes the application, not the underlying rules.
